issues.display_title: Issue #2030: fix(payment): add null guard and nullable type to getStripeSubscriptionDetail to prevent TypeError crashes
issues.main_description_html:
Context & Problem

During the 60-day payment failure audit (Issue #2023, REC-04), a fatal PHP TypeError was recorded in ccdb.cc_logs (Log ID 108187) on 2026-09-28 for User 31611:

App\Http\Controllers\Payment\Helpers\PaymentHelpers::getStripeSubscriptionDetail(): 
Argument #2 ($recurringProfile) must be of type string, null given, 
called in Upgrade.php on line 126

In PaymentHelpers.php, the method signature is declared as:

public function getStripeSubscriptionDetail($stripeClient, string $recurringProfile)

Because the type declaration requires string (non-nullable), passing null immediately triggers a fatal TypeError (HTTP 500) before the function's internal validation if (empty($recurringProfile)) can execute.

This occurs in Upgrade.php, Downgrade.php, and SpaceAddon.php when a user attempts to change plans without an existing active recurring subscription profile (or when changing to photo_studio where recurring_profile_photo_studio is null in user_extra_data).

Scope of Work

  1. Nullable Parameter Declaration:
    • Update getStripeSubscriptionDetail signature in app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Helpers/PaymentHelpers.php to accept ?string $recurringProfile.
    • Ensure the internal empty($recurringProfile) check catches null/empty strings and throws a graceful business exception (HTTP 409 Conflict).
  2. Defensive Early Guards in Action Controllers:
    • Add early validation guards in:
      • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Stripe/Subscription/Upgrade.php
      • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Stripe/Subscription/Downgrade.php
      • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Stripe/Subscription/SpaceAddon.php
    • Immediately throw an HTTP 409 exception with clear message if $recurringProfile is absent before attempting Stripe subscription retrieval.
  3. Automated Unit Testing:
    • Add unit test coverage in tests/Unit/Payment/PaymentHelpersTest.php verifying that getStripeSubscriptionDetail safely handles null and throws the expected exception without fatal TypeError.

Acceptance Criteria

  • getStripeSubscriptionDetail accepts nullable string (?string $recurringProfile).
  • Passing null throws a standard business exception (HTTP 409) rather than an unhandled PHP 500 TypeError.
  • Upgrade, Downgrade, and SpaceAddon action controllers safely validate $recurringProfile presence.
  • Unit tests pass with 100% pass rate.

Result

  • PR: #2057 (fix(payment): add null guard and nullable type to getStripeSubscriptionDetail (#2030))
  • Key Commit: b938e333c
  • Testing Verification:
    • vendor/bin/phpunit tests/Unit/Payment/PaymentHelpersTest.php executed under SQLite in-memory guard (guardProductionConnections).
    • Output: 8 tests, 16 assertions passed (100% pass rate).

issues.display_title: Issue #2066: Default Stripe test clock ON for Stripe test users in subscribe flow
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

POST /v2/payment/subscription/subs only attaches a Stripe test clock when ?test_clock=true is passed in the query string. It is easy to miss, so test customers end up without a clock (e.g. sub_1UQ22A4UXotNjjkIkKniryTE). A test clock cannot be attached after the customer is created, which blocks reproducing renewal scenarios (billing_reason = subscription_cycle → past_due → card update → upgrade).

Change

For users in HelperClass::getStripeTestUserIds() (Stripe test mode), default test_clock to true when the param is absent. ?test_clock=false still opts out. Live users are unaffected.

Acceptance Criteria

  • AC-001 Test user, no param → test clock created and attached to the customer
  • AC-002 Test user, ?test_clock=false → no clock
  • AC-003 Test user, ?test_clock=true → clock created
  • AC-004 Live user, no param → no clock (unchanged)
  • AC-005 Live user, ?test_clock=true → rejected (existing guard)
  • AC-006 Invalid values (foo, 1, yes, on) still rejected
  • AC-007 Existing tests pass; new tests added

Notes

  • Test-clock customers do not renew in real time; the clock must be advanced manually.
  • Stripe limits test clocks per account and customers per clock; old clocks need periodic cleanup. Deleting a clock also deletes its customers/subscriptions.
